title: Oranexus reseller & hybrid GPU onboarding discovery
customer_attendees: Diego Alvarez - Head of Cloud Engineering
summary: Introductory partner discovery between Redwood AE/SE and Oranexus Partnerships + Cloud eng. Discussed reseller model, hybrid GPU routing, private/VPC deployment patterns, billing/marketplace options, and high-level security/compliance requirements. Agreed on pilot scope: co-bill proof-of-concept with routing tests in APAC region and a short benchmarking exercise on cost/latency tradeoffs.
topics: security: SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS/HSM, audit logs
action_items: Maya Patel: Share partner one-pager + proposed reseller pricing matrix (due 2026-05-20)
Liam Chen: Draft technical checklist for Oranexus private deployment (VPC peering, peering bandwidth, KMS integration) and send initial runbook (due 2026-05-21)
Priya Rao: Provide target customer segments and expected monthly usage ranges (due 2026-05-18)
Diego Alvarez: Confirm APAC region endpoints and any on-prem GPU SKUs to test (due 2026-05-19)
Tom Becker: Introduce Redwood legal to Oranexus procurement for standard reseller agreement (no date yet, aim next week)
next_steps: Schedule 60m technical deep-dive with Oranexus infra team (SE-led) for week of 2026-05-25

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-14 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Diego (Oranexus Head Cloud), Priya (Oranexus Partnerships), Tom (CTO)

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. quick intro from our side, im maya, AE on the channel team. liam is our se, he'll jump into the technical bits.
[00:12] Diego: Hi thanks, Diego here. excited to talk about how we might resell and integrate hybrid GPU routing.
[00:18] Priya: Priya from partnerships. high level we want a clean onramp for our customers into hybrid gpu offerings and co-billing options.
[00:26] Liam: cool, i'll give a quick overview of redwood's serving modes — hosted api, dedicated pools and private vpc/on prem. i'll try not to get too deep at first.
[00:37] Tom: that sounds good. our concerns are primarily around latency for APAC customers and being able to hold data in-region for certain regulated customers.
[00:44] Maya: noted. quick question on your side: are you thinking marketplace listing + reseller billing or more of a technical OEM integration?
[00:52] Priya: probably both? we do want to list on our marketplace but also offer managed bundles where we manage the infra and bill our customers directly.
[00:59] Liam: okay so two flows — marketplace discovery where redwood is a model endpoint and direct co-bill where orinexus operates dedicated pools for customers. from a tech standpoint routing policies can send requests to hosted redwood endpoints or to your dedicated private deployment.
[01:12] Diego: how does the routing work if say we have a customer in singapore and your hosted endpoints also have an APAC region? do we prefer local dedicated GPU first then fallback?
[01:23] Liam: yes, policy-based. we support priority rules: prefer local private pool, fallback to hosted in the same region, then cross-region. it does require capacity mapping — we can tag model variants and regions. sometimes the transcript generator picks up "prefetch" as "precache" so please excuse fuzziness.
[01:42] Priya: got it. on the billing side, is there attribution for usage per-customer so we can reconcile monthly invoices?
[01:50] Maya: yes, we emit token-level usage metrics per API key and you can map keys to Oranexus customer IDs. for reseller co-billing we can produce consolidated invoices and also provide line-item exports.
[02:04] Tom: are those exports S3 dumps or through the partner portal?
[02:08] Maya: both. portal has dashboards and csv downloads, and we can stream usage to your billing S3 bucket or push via webhook.
[02:15] Diego: circling back to private deployments — what does KMS integration look like? we need to ensure customer keys are managed in our HSM.
[02:23] Liam: we support customer-managed keys via standard KMS integrations — we have examples for AWS KMS and on-prem HSM. note: some words get garbled in the transcript, like K V cash — but i mean K V cache and KMS integration.
[02:36] Priya: and for compliance, do you have SOC2 and ISO stuff we can share with our legal?
[02:40] Maya: yes, SOC2 type II, ISO 27001 artifacts available. we'll attach the security pack but legal will likely ask for audit logs retention policy — we keep audit trails for 13 months by default but enterprise plans can extend.
[02:55] Tom: good. what about SSO for portal access? SAML?
[02:58] Liam: SAML and OIDC both supported, SCIM for provisioning. RBAC roles are configurable per partner/reseller.
[03:07] Diego: performance — do you have benchmark numbers for throughput per GPU SKU? we use a mix of A-series and forthcoming G-series cards on prem.
[03:16] Liam: we publish verified profiles for common open models; for private fleets, we recommend doing a short benchmark. latency depends a lot on seq length, batching and KV cache warm state. we can run a 48-hour benchmark with your SKUs as part of the pilot.
[03:31] Priya: that would be helpful. we want to show customers predictable pricing across dedicated vs hosted.
[03:36] Maya: which leads to model variants — we can supply quantized variants that reduce token cost with modest quality tradeoffs. part of the pilot can test quality thresholds.
[03:45] Tom: what's the typical fallback behavior when capacity is exhausted in a dedicated pool?
[03:50] Liam: automatic fallback to compatible hosted variants; you can configure strict routing where requests are rejected vs soft routing with fallback. in soft mode we add a header to signal the fallback and you can monitor quality.
[04:03] Diego: latency SLOs?
[04:05] Liam: for dedicated pools we offer SLOs depending on commit — e.g., p95 under 300ms for small-gen workloads on certain SKUs. hosted endpoints have documented latencies per model. we can share a performance matrix.
[04:20] Priya: marketplace listing — what metadata do you require for a marketplace tile? screenshots, pricing tiers, compliance badges?
[04:28] Maya: yes, typical: product tile, short description, pricing link, supported regions, compliance badges (SOC2/ISO), contact details, and support SLAs. we'll send a marketplace requirements doc.
[04:38] Diego: question: are there any exclusivity or channel protections? we have existing partners in EMEA and want to avoid conflicts.
[04:45] Maya: we don't force exclusivity but we can discuss territory language in the reseller agreement. that's a legal conversation; we'll loop in procurement.
[04:53] Tom: security again — for air-gapped customers, can you support an on-prem appliance?
[04:58] Liam: yes, we have an on-prem package. some customers run a private control plane with network isolation; those installs require a bit more ops support.
[05:07] Priya: what about upgrades and model rollouts? as a reseller we may want to control when we expose new model versions to our customers.
[05:15] Liam: rollouts can be canaryed per route or per API key. you can pin customers to specific model versions and we support automatic fallback to previous versions if quality degrades.
[05:26] Diego: how do we instrument multi-tenant usage on a single private pool? any tenant isolation concerns?
[05:33] Liam: we recommend namespace-level rate limiting + KV cache partitioning. memory isolation is enforced at process level; multi-tenancy is supported but for high-security customers we advise separate pools.
[05:43] Speaker 1: "we also did ask about service fees"
[05:45] Maya: pricing is flexible — per-token plus a management fee for reseller bundles. we'll propose a couple of models: revenue share vs margin-based markup.
[05:56] Priya: for the co-bill pilot what does success look like?
[06:00] Tom: we want to validate latency in APAC <350ms p95, accurate usage attribution, and a clean billing reconciliation flow.
[06:09] Liam: sounds reasonable. we can provision a small dedicated pool in APAC for the pilot and run a set of synthetic and real traffic tests.
[06:18] Diego: sync frequency during pilot? weekly check-ins?
[06:21] Maya: weekly standups and a shared spreadsheet for issues. we'll also do an initial technical deep-dive with your infra team.
[06:29] Priya: can you also provide a sample reseller agreement?
[06:32] Maya: yes, legal will share a redlined template; tom you can intro procurement and we'll loop in contracts.
[06:38] Tom: will do.
[06:40] Liam: one more nit — model quantization and quality monitoring. we have eval hooks tied to prompt sets so you can detect regressions during rollouts. it's useful if you have customer-specific prompts.
[06:52] Diego: that could be a selling point.
[06:54] Speaker 2 (misc): "uh huh"
[06:55] Maya: ok summarizing next steps: maya shares partner one-pager and marketplace doc, liam shares private deployment checklist, priya shares usage ranges, diego confirms regions/sku, tom intros procurement. schedule se deep dive for week of 5/25.
[07:12] Priya: perfect thanks everyone. look forward to the technical call.
[07:16] Maya: thank you all, we'll follow up with calendar invites and the docs. bye.

Notes: transcript contains some ASR noise; occasional words like "K V cash" instead of "KV cache" and speaker mislabels. Links referenced during call: Redwood partner portal: https://partners.redwood.ai/portal (reference), Marketplace requirements doc (link shared in follow-up email).
closing_notes: Call ended with clear pilot scope and owner assignments. Plan: technical deep-dive + pilot SOW. Legal loop to start for reseller agreement.
file_notes: Link to partner docs will be attached to CRM ticket ORX-2026-PART-1423. Transcript included as-is; some speaker labels generic.
